_doc: Lead, step 3 (2026-10-24). Neutral-equivalence bisection. Each row: candidate vs the unchanged original on A's equivalence fixtures (tests/fixtures/teacher/schedule.json first 6 maps x both sides, opponent original; official CLI --release default fuel). n_equal = cells whose replay and summary are byte-identical to the original-vs-original reference. Tool: tools/lead_neutral_bisect.py, tools/audit_equivalence.py.

teacher_exact (all heads compiled out).note: wasm byte-identical to the original; equality is by construction

conclusions: The original teacher is chaotically sensitive to tiny fuel shifts that happen BEFORE or DURING its decisions: ~40 fuel at turn start changes 2/12 cells (the fuel-dependent search depth/admission reads are continuous in remaining fuel). Spend AFTER its decisions is harmless (13.5k end-of-turn burn: 24/24 identical).

Consequently a fuel-credit mechanism must be exact to the instruction to give byte-identical play. It cannot be: even the credit arithmetic inside teacher_left() (one load + add per read) shifts fuel and reduces equality from 11/12 to 6/12. The credit makes neutrality WORSE, not better.
Confirmed: diagnosis-phase-2 finding 1 (zero head != neutral) is a general property of this teacher, not only of the old camp-net feature ordering.

Design decision: (1) the neutral *control arm* for every future evaluation is an overhead-matched build of the same binary with heads in shadow/zero-residual (neutral_real), never the bare original; (2) teacher_exact remains the only byte-exact equivalence claim; (3) neural work that runs before teacher decisions is kept minimal and fixed-cost (captures noinline), and records/telemetry run after play_turn; (4) kFuelCredit is kept only as an experimental flag and is not claimed as a neutrality proof.
